method: Read from REALITY.md (site v0.1.258), CLAUDE.md, the code and data files, the passes and guidance in board/, and the live site https://promptugal.news (GET only, status codes checked; the live version string was v0.1.258, the same as REALITY.md). The gate and the tests were not re-run in this read; their results are as the repository states them. Maturity: runs = works today with evidence; partial = works with a named gap; designed = not running.

items.name: The static publishing machine (build, gate, CI-owned version, one-command release)
items.one_line: A website generator with no dependencies that turns markdown and JSON into a full site, refuses to publish if the checks fail, numbers every release automatically and shows the version on every page.
items.buyer_says: I want to publish a website like this one, where every change is checked and versioned and nobody can ship a broken or unsourced page.
what_works: node newsroom/build/build.mjs turns content/ (markdown) and data/ (JSON) into pages, markdown twins, llms.txt, sitemap and the JSON API; Node 18+, no npm dependencies

A small core plus one module per section in newsroom/build/features/ (about 40 feature files); a new section is one file plus at most one line in data/site/nav.json; the contract is newsroom/build/README.md

The gate, newsroom/build/validate.js, builds once and must print OK: schema validation of every data file, every reference between entities, derived files fresh, every page has page-type and page-date, no contact details in content or data, no leaked key shapes, article title length, signed articles, vendored files hash-checked, theme colour tokens complete, and a ratchet that stops code files from holding more prose than their baseline

CI (.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml) runs the gate on every push and pull request; on a push to dev, newsroom/build/tag_release.sh numbers the release, writes the version into version.txt, versions.json and REALITY.md, builds, runs the gate again, commits as GitHub Actions, tags and deploys to GitHub Pages
newsroom/tools/release.sh: rebases on dev, re-derives data, runs the gate locally so a red gate never leaves the machine, pushes, then waits until the live site serves the new version
Live: 879+ pages at https://promptugal.news, release history page, 474 commits and 258 numbered releases in one working week
A version badge at the top of every page and an agent block at the end
items.how_to_see_it: https://promptugal.news/newsroom/versions.html (every release, numbered by CI) and newsroom/build/README.md in the repository
depends_on: Node 18+
a GitHub repository with Pages enabled and Actions
a domain with DNS pointed at GitHub Pages (the live site has this working)
items.open_source: Code Apache-2.0 (LICENSE and README.md state it); text CC BY 4.0. The release and tag scripts are stated to be copied from the team's own earlier site (SGit-AI/SGit-AI__Website__Web-Summit).
buyer_would_need_made: Replace the site's content, data schemas, navigation and brand with the buyer's
Decide which of the gate's checks apply (the contact-detail and no-em-dash rules are this publication's policy, not universal)
Point CI and the domain at the buyer's repository and Pages setup; train the buyer's people on the commit convention and the release script
Remove or keep the agent-run team features (run ledger, board, desks) depending on whether the buyer runs agents

package_ideas.scope: Stand up the machine in the buyer's repository with their brand shell, one content section and the gate green, with a one-hour hand-over call.
Starter plus a data-driven section (for example their products or events), custom checks in the gate, the release script rolled out to their editors, and a runbook.
A full publication on the machine: data model, several sections, JSON API, markdown twins, signed articles, CI and domain, with a month of support.

gaps: The tests (search, chat, meter, vault, browser) are run by hand; CI runs only the gate
REALITY.md still lists 'not yet': branch protection on main, the review/ folder and an Agent Contact file from the estate standard
The system assumes agents and one repository; a buyer with a conventional editorial team would not use the board, desks or hourly-run parts
Some worker branches were seen to cause cancelled or untagged deploys (two releases on dev have no tag, per a comment in tag_release.sh); CI hardening is ongoing

items.name: The site that AI agents and search engines can read (twins, llms.txt, JSON API, signed articles)
items.one_line: Every page also exists as clean markdown, every entity as JSON, with llms.txt, sitemaps, an RSS feed, search-engine metadata and signed articles, all generated, never hand-kept.
items.buyer_says: I want my site to be easy for ChatGPT, Claude and Google to read, and I want my articles signed so people can tell they are really ours.
what_works: A markdown twin for every page (same path with .md), generated from the same content so the two cannot drift
llms.txt grouped by section, sitemap.xml with lastmod, news-sitemap.xml, feed.xml (RSS, latest 50 articles), robots.txt naming both sitemaps

A JSON API under /api/v1/: an index, a file per entity (120 companies, 235 events, 264 people, 223 organisations, 80 places, 17 topics, 39 stories, 33 captures), graphs, the ontology, search documents and a manifest listing every file's SHA-256 and schema
Open Graph, Twitter card and JSON-LD (NewsMediaOrganization, WebSite with SearchAction, NewsArticle, BreadcrumbList) on pages; noindex on the sign-in page and the 404

Articles signed by the publisher's key; the gate refuses an unsigned article and checks each signature against the public key register (board/keys.json); a sign-article tool makes a signature that survives version bumps
The site is a verified property in Google Search Console with the sitemap read (2026-11-06, 979 discovered pages, per REALITY.md)
depends_on: the static publishing machine
a key register for article signing (the repository's own board/keys.json and the pki-agent tool from pki.sgit.ai)
items.open_source: Code Apache-2.0; the API's own index states data CC BY 4.0, code Apache-2.0
buyer_would_need_made: Map the buyer's entities to API files and schemas
Set up the buyer's signing keys and register
Adjust JSON-LD types and organisation details to the buyer
Submit feeds to Search Console and any news programmes

items.name: The sourced knowledge graph: entities as JSON folders with schemas, an ontology, derived data and re-checks
items.one_line: A way to keep what you know about companies, people, events and places as plain JSON files, each fact with its source link and the date it was read, checked by schema, and joined into one graph.
items.buyer_says: I want a database of my market (companies, people, events) where every fact has a source and a date and nothing unsourced can get published.
what_works: One folder per entity (companies, places, topics, events, people, organisations, evidence captures, story projects), JSON only, 24 schemas in data/schemas/, checked by the gate
An ontology (data/ontology.json): 13 types in four worlds and 20 verbs, each with a distinct inverse and a list of forbidden verbs; the gate holds every graph to its grammar

Hand-edited versus derived files kept apart: derived entities (events, people, organisations, evidence, stories) are written by newsroom/tools/derive.mjs from desk files, committed so changes arrive as reviewable diffs, and the gate fails if they are stale

Companies as five-file folders (company, sources, facts, edges, recheck): each field names its supporting sources, each source carries url, read date, who read it and what it supports; a re-check log is appended, never rewritten; 120 companies live on the API
Public-fields-only import from a team CRM record, leaving out the team's private notes (data/README.md rule 6)
Story project folders (sources, entities, claims marked fact, estimate or opinion, graph, timeline, blocks) with citations resolved by the gate
A name-matching report (data/matching.json) listing matches, refused near misses and unmatched names, so data quality is visible
A multi-model fact re-check tool (newsroom/tools/verify/verify.mjs) with 11 article records and a /newsroom/verification/ page
evidence: https://promptugal.news/api/v1/index.json (200: counts of 120 companies, 235 events, 264 people, 223 organisations)
items.how_to_see_it: https://promptugal.news/api/ for the data and https://promptugal.news/companies/ for the profiles built from it; data/README.md for the layout
depends_on: Node 18+
the build and gate
a human or agent to read sources and write the source records
items.open_source: Code Apache-2.0; data CC BY 4.0 per the API index. The facts are public facts about companies with source links, not the team's private notes.
buyer_would_need_made: Design the buyer's ontology (their entity types and verbs) and schemas
Load their existing records into the folder format and write the derivation for their desks or feeds
Choose which sources count and set the re-check cadence
Decide on matching rules for names

package_ideas.scope: A schema and folder layout for one entity type from the buyer's data, with sources and read dates, validated by a gate.
A small ontology (about 5 types, 10 verbs), a derivation from their spreadsheets or CRM, the gate, and a JSON API.
A full sourced knowledge base for their market (hundreds of entities), with a re-check routine, a matching report, a verification pass and the graph on top.

gaps: Re-checks are a tool option run by hand (companies.mjs --recheck); nothing re-checks automatically on a schedule
Vault capture ids and SHA-256 fields on company sources are empty: no capture is tied to a source yet
Company flows (how AI agents sit in a company's work) are mapped for only a few companies so far
No graph file per organisation, place or topic yet; the search files have no schema
The fact re-check pipeline: 11 records exist, but how often models agree or catch real errors has not been published in what was read
Quality depends on the people or agents reading sources; the structure does not guarantee a fact is right

items.name: The graph explorer
items.one_line: An interactive map of everything in the data: start from a company, a session or a person, expand outward, filter, rank, and ask 'how is A connected to B?' with the answer read as sentences with sources.
items.buyer_says: I want to explore my market as a graph and answer how two companies or people are connected, in the browser, with no backend.
what_works: The explorer at /graph/: 1,642 nodes and 2,828 edges on the live page in four worlds; starts from a question (the most central nodes, a node, a view, or a path), never the whole graph
Explore walk by hops, depth stepper, pinned anchors, top N nodes or edges by PageRank, betweenness or degree, filters by world, type, verb and facet (day, organiser, field, country)
Layouts: force, a map computed at build (so the whole graph draws in about half a second), radial, layered, tree, grid, list
Up to three shortest routes between two nodes, read as sentences with their sources and read dates
State kept in the URL so a view can be shared; a panel with the node's record
Small prerendered graphs on company, event, person, organisation and topic pages with 'Open in the graph'
Ported from graphs.sgit.ai's universe reader (stated as Apache-2.0) with Cytoscape.js 3.30.2 vendored with its MIT licence; the gate checks the explorer file matches the whole graph edge for edge
Page tools for chat control of the graph (load, focus, expand, filter, path, snapshot)
Also live: an animated 'centres of gravity' view (/graph/gravity/) and a world map of companies (/graph/world/), both returned 200
depends_on: the knowledge graph data
the build (computes ranks and the map layout at build time)
Cytoscape.js (vendored)
items.open_source: Site code Apache-2.0; Cytoscape.js vendored under MIT with its licence in assets/vendor/cytoscape/; the port's origin is stated in REALITY.md as graphs.sgit.ai (Apache-2.0)

items.name: Reading meter, account and pay-as-you-read top-up (with the reader vault)
items.one_line: A meter in the reader's browser that prices each page by its kind and how fresh it is, never blocks reading, and lets the reader top up credit through a Stripe payment link, with a vault (beta) for keeping the history.
items.buyer_says: I want readers to pay a little for what they read, with prices that depend on the kind of page and how new it is, without a paywall and without tracking them.
what_works: sg-meter v1.5.0, vendored unedited with its hashes checked by the gate, with this site's storage key
One file, data/billing/prices.json, makes both the meter's config (/api/v1/billing/meter.json) and the published price table (/account/billing.html), so the table and the meter cannot disagree

Pricing: a base per page type (article 6, briefing 5, analysis 3, story 2, evidence 1, site 1, account 0 on a pence-scale credit) times a freshness tier (fresh x2, new x1.5, current x1, archive x0.5), times the share of the page actually read, never under a tenth; once per page per session; starts at 5.00 pounds; never blocking; balance can go below zero; a reader can rate to re-price or decline and say why
Everything stays in the reader's browser; no account is needed to read
Account pages (/account/: balance, history, receipts, export as JSON, restore) and a top-up page with a live Stripe Payment Link for 5.00 pounds
Features billing.mjs and account.mjs; a Node test for the pricing rules and a Chromium test of reading, the account, the top-up and the return (run by hand)
Reader vault (beta): sign in with a passkey, vault client sg-vault v0.2.3 vendored; tested against a mock vault server

items.name: Browser search and 'Ask the site' chat with the reader's own key
items.one_line: Instant search over every page from a small sharded index in the browser, plus a chat that answers from the site's own data using the reader's own OpenRouter key, which never leaves their browser, showing every step.

what_works: A sharded search index built at release: docs.json (one row per page with facets) plus 328 term shards; weighted by field with accent folding, light stemming, prefix matching and synonyms drawn from the data (company aliases, tracks, places); a query loads one docs file and one to three shards (under 7 KB)
Search button with instant dropdown (the slash key focuses it) and a /search/ page with facets and ?q=
Page tool API (window.__tool) with read, view and author levels, JSON Schema parameters and an interaction log, so any page tool can be used by a chat

Ask pane with the reader's OpenRouter key kept only in their browser and sent only to openrouter.ai, a Forget key button, a model picker (default anthropic/claude-sonnet-5), a tool loop showing every call and result, and a no-key mode that runs tools by hand
Tests: search.test.mjs (index size, query bytes), chat.test.mjs (the loop against a mocked OpenRouter), browser.check.cjs (Chromium)
Search and Ask pages return 200 live

for Ask: the reader's own OpenRouter account and key
the page tool API

items.name: Article images and infographics (code-drawn set and AI-model set with a logged ladder of models)
items.one_line: A way to give every article its own infographic in several styles and sizes, drawn from the article's own facts word for word, with an option to have AI image models make the picture from the whole article at a recorded cost.
items.buyer_says: I want a branded infographic or cartoon for every article, using only the facts in the article, at a cost I can see.
what_works: A code-drawn set: design/infographics/make.mjs (Chromium via Playwright) turns articles.json (each figure and point keeps the exact sentence it came from) into three layouts (figure, network, timeline), two styles (paper, ink) and three sizes (thumb, card, banner); 61 files committed in design/infographics/out/ (10 articles by 2 styles by 3 sizes plus an index)

An AI-model route: design/ai-images/gen.mjs sends the whole article to an image model through OpenRouter with the brand palette and strict rules (facts only from the article, exact spelling, no faces, no company logos, a footer marking the picture as AI-made); three styles in styles.json (editorial, cartoon, explainer)
Each call is logged to a vault outside the repository: model, style, prompt hash, cost from the provider's own usage figure, seconds, bytes and file; the key is read from the environment only

A ladder of models with prices read on 6 November (gemini-3.1-flash-lite-image about 0.03 USD, gemini-3.1-flash-image 0.07, gemini-3-pro-image 0.15), cheapest first for drafts and the top one for the image that ships; at most 3 tries per image; a daily budget set by the accountant (10 USD until Dinis decides)
The designer's session note records that the Pro model got every figure right first time on the whole-article prompt
evidence: board/budgets.json (the OpenRouter section: ladder, tries, daily budget)

items.name: Wikipedia read as data (pinned revisions, statements by wording, findings for an editor)
items.one_line: A tool that reads a Wikipedia article at a fixed revision into structured files (every sentence classed by how it is worded, every reference, tables and links), joins it to your graph, and lists weak points for a person to take to the article's talk page.
items.buyer_says: I want to use Wikipedia as a structured, citable data source for my sector and see where it is wrong or thin, without ever editing it by machine.
what_works: newsroom/tools/wikipedia.mjs reads one English Wikipedia article through the MediaWiki API (named user agent, no key) and writes article.json, statements.json, references.json, tables.json and links.json; no editor's name is kept
Statements are classed by wording (record, stated, attributed, quote, hedged), never by whether they are true

One article read: Web Summit at revision 1383690798, with 79 statements, 63 references, a 17-row timeline table and 373 links; 14 links meet entities in the graph and 15 timeline rows became past-edition events
Five findings recorded for a person (W-01 to W-05: for example no 2025 row though the organiser published dates, nothing on 2026, 30 of 79 sentences uncited)
Six wikipedia schemas checked by the gate; two taxonomies added to the ontology (article kind, source provenance)
Rules of engagement: never edit Wikipedia, pin the revision (the revision id is the attribution under CC BY-SA 4.0), privacy first

items.name: Operations dashboard and quality pages built from data
items.one_line: Back-office pages generated at each release from the team's own files and git history: who worked when, what waits on a person, a run ledger, the release history, and a measure of how much prose still sits inside code.
items.buyer_says: I want a live view of what my team and my agents are doing, what is blocked and waiting on me, and whether our content is really kept in data rather than in code.
what_works: /newsroom/dashboard/: a load, extract, transform, save cycle at every build over board/schedule.json, each agent's status.json, any hold file, the story board and the last 24 hours of git commits, producing a row per agent, a grid of wakes by hour, what waits on Dinis oldest first and the hand-offs; the clock and next wakes run live in the browser
The same model as an API file (api/v1/newsroom/dashboard.json) and a status file (api/v1/newsroom/status.json)

The control centre: overview, every run (filterable), agents, a swim-lane timeline by agent, the data and its sources and read dates, workflows, a lab, release history and decision pages for the owner
A runs ledger (data/newsroom/runs/<day>.jsonl) written by a tool, one line per commit
The quality page (/newsroom/quality/): measures every build where code files hold prose or HTML in strings (about 120 KB in 68 files at the start) and the gate's ratchet only lets that number go down
Charts are SVG drawn at build time; no page needs a script apart from the live clock
Dashboard, quality, data, runs, timeline, desks, versions, workflows and verification pages all returned 200 live
depends_on: the build
a roster, schedule and status.json per agent or team member
commit trailers (Agent, For, To) in the team's git convention
buyer_would_need_made: Map the buyer's team, roles and status file format
Choose what counts as 'waits on me' for their owner
Adapt commit conventions or swap to their tracker
Decide which pages are public: here they are public for now by choice

gaps: The runs ledger and the team-site snapshot are not kept current automatically: the conductor runs the tools by hand before a release, so a release's own commit appears at the next one
The builders' branches show no run until merged
Time is HEAD's commit time, so the dashboard is only as fresh as the last release
Most of it assumes the agent-team conventions of this project
The quality page measures where prose sits in code but cannot judge whether content is good

items.name: Backup and recovery plan with a restore-tested repository bundle
items.one_line: A verified full backup of the whole repository as one file, proven by cloning it and running the site's checks on the clone, with a written plan for what else must be saved and how it is restored.
items.buyer_says: I want to know my site and its data can be restored from a backup, and that the backup has been tested, not just made.
what_works: tools/backup.sh makes a git bundle of all refs and a manifest (head, SHA-256, size); it now unshallows first, clones the bundle, compares heads and runs fsck, because an earlier shallow clone produced a bundle that passed 'verify' yet was incomplete (a defect the agent found and recorded)
A full bundle (774 commits, about 78 MB) was restored by clone and the gate printed OK on the clone (v0.1.237); an incremental bundle was 4.9 MB

plan.md: assets, tiers (repository, media vaults, deltas, destination), encryption rules (a vault archive keeps ciphertext, keys never stored beside it), verification and restore steps, and asks; security's review added: never read the agents' secret folders, and run the gate on a restored clone
A Google Drive folder was created with Dinis's word and a manifest uploaded as the record of each backup (the plan page returned 200 live)
depends_on: git and a place to keep the bundle
for vault backups: read access from each vault's holder
for Drive: a connector or credential granted by the owner
items.open_source: Script and plan live in the repository under its Apache-2.0 licence
buyer_would_need_made: The buyer's own list of assets that cannot be lost
A durable destination and credentials
A schedule (the plan proposes every 6 hours and after major releases) and restore drills
Vault or database backup for anything beyond git

package_ideas.scope: Install the backup script, a restore test and a one-page plan for the buyer's repository.

A full backup and recovery programme for the site, its media and any encrypted vaults, with deltas and key-loss planning.

gaps: The bundle cannot be sent to Drive through the connector (it would pass through the model); only manifests reach Drive. A shell upload credential, a person pulling a clone or a vault lane is needed
No vault has been backed up: the backup agent holds no vault key, and security's per-vault recovery steps were still awaited
The scheduled run and a durable destination for the bundle are not in place; bundles lived in the container only
The connected Drive belongs to an agent account; whether it is the intended place was awaiting Dinis
Deltas and encrypted vault archives are planned, not built
